items.stem: How do security groups differ from network ACLs in a VPC?

options.text: Security groups are stateful; NACLs are stateless
options.rationale: Correct: security groups track connection state; NACLs evaluate each direction independently.

options.text: Security groups are stateless; NACLs are stateful

items.explanation: Correct: security groups are stateful, NACLs stateless.

items.stem: Which TWO are reasons to use a Transit Gateway over many point-to-point VPC peerings? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It provides transitive routing among many VPCs
options.rationale: Correct: Transit Gateway hubs connectivity transitively.

options.text: It simplifies routing as the number of VPCs grows
options.rationale: Correct: a hub-and-spoke avoids an N-squared mesh of peerings.
Transit Gateway has its own data/attachment charges.

options.text: It removes the need for CIDR planning

items.explanation: Correct: Transit Gateway gives transitive routing and simpler scaling.

items.stem: What makes a subnet effectively 'public' in a VPC?

options.text: A route to an internet gateway in its route table
options.rationale: Correct: the route to the IGW makes a subnet public.
The name has no effect on routing.
Security groups do not create internet routing.

items.explanation: Correct: a route to an IGW makes a subnet public.
